key_findings: FINDING-1 VRAM CEILING VERIFIED: WSL Issue #40732 (wzgrx, 2026-06-06) attests WSL2 GPU-PV OOM is NOT recoverable - consecutive allocation failures corrupt GPU-PV translation layer -> Hyper-V VM kernel panic -> Windows BSOD requiring full reboot. BodyText eval confirms 'CUDA OOM should return cudaErrorMemoryAllocation... Instead ... VM kernel panics'. For gfx1100 RX 7900 XT with 20GB, Qwen3 27B IQ4_XS ~15.3GB + KV cache at 8k (~2.5-3.6GB for 32 layers, 128 heads) = 17.8-18.9GB leaves <1.1GB headroom; single fragmented mmap or second model load triggers same OOM path as #40732. Related #40401 shows 16 GiB invisible DXGI/Hyper-V overhead on Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000 96GB) where mem_get_info reports 80+ GiB free but contiguous alloc fails at 3.48 GiB - directly contradicts WSL2 spec of 'full VRAM passthrough'. Flag conflicting evidence: AMD DXG path may differ from NVIDIA CUDA path, but DXG translation layer is shared - risk remains.

FINDING-2 20GB LIMIT MATH: ROCm GPU specs page (tab8, rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/reference/gpu-specs.html) lists ONLY Instinct MI300/MI250 series; NO Radeon RX 7000 / gfx1100 entry - confirms ROCm 10.0.0 does not officially document RDNA3 consumer support. This matches prior observation that gfx1100 is community-supported via gfx1100 via HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION, not validated. Model IQ4_XS 15.3GB cited in task: at 8k context, llama.cpp default KV uses fp16 (2 bytes * 2 (K+V) * n_layers * n_ctx * d_model). For Qwen 27B (approx 32 layers, 4608 hidden), 8192 * 32 * 2 * 2 * 4608 ≈ 3.2 GB. Sum 18.5GB -> 1.5GB left for buffers/graph allocations. At 32k, KV alone ~12.8GB -> 28GB > 20GB guaranteed OOM. No conflicting source found that claims 20GB is safe at 8k; WSL troubleshooting page (tab16) contains zero guidance on VRAM overcommit.

FINDING-3 BANDWIDTH ROOFLINE 800GB/s: RDNA3 Wikipedia (tab10) reports Memory support GDDR6 up to 20 Gbps, PCIe 4.0, InFO-RDL chiplet interconnect 5.3 TB/s intra-die but external memory bandwidth bounded: RX 7900 XT = 20GB GDDR6 @ 20 Gbps * 320-bit /8 = 800 GB/s (5 MCDs *64-bit), RX 7900 XTX = 960 GB/s (6 MCDs). Prefill is memory-bandwidth bound: tokens/s ≈ bandwidth / (2 * model_size_bytes / n_ctx) for attention? More directly, prefill FLOPS: attention QK^T is O(n^2 d): at 8k, 8192^2 ≈ 67M elements per layer *32 ≈ 2.1B operations vs 2k context 4M*32=128M -> 16x increase. Bandwidth roof: 800 GB/s / 15.3GB model = 52 passes/sec theoretical max, but quadratic attention blows cache residency: InfCache 96MB L3 stated in RDNA3 page ('L3 Infinity Cache up to 96MB... latency increased as physically on MCDs') vs 8k KV 3.2GB >> cache -> every layer streams from GDDR6. 1000 tok/s would require 1000*15.3GB =15.3 TB/s memory movement if naive - impossible. Even optimized FlashAttention reduces to ~1-2x model size, still > 15 TB/s needed. No source contradicts this; ROCm docs (tab6) claim 'optimized for Instinct' not Radeon.

FINDING-4 THERMAL 90C ABORTS: No direct thermal doc found in visited pages (ROCm docs omit consumer thermal policy, Wikipedia RDNA3 mentions power efficiency 54% perf/watt but not TJmax). However, WSL troubleshooting page (tab16) and ROCm specs (tab8) show 'AMD GPU system optimization' link exists but not scraped - suggests thermal management is host-side (Windows driver), not visible to WSL. Contrarian inference: RX 7900 XT reference T_junction 110C, throttling starts at 90C hotspot in practice (community reports, not in scraped docs - flagged as uncertain). Sustained 1000 tok/s prefill at 8k will saturate 300W+ board power; WSL2 DXG adds extra shim copies -> power virus conditions. Failure mode: clock decoupling front-end 2.5GHz / shaders 2.3GHz (Wikipedia) will throttle shader clock first, collapsing prefill throughput without warning, then driver TDR if sustained. Cannot profile via WSL to detect.

FINDING-5 WSL2 JITTER FLATTENING 1.0x: Direct evidence from #40401 eval: 'identical 16 GiB overhead' across driver versions, 'NOT a NVIDIA driver bug - it's WSL2 virtualization layer behavior.' DXG paravirtualization adds 2 layers: DXGI shim (/usr/lib/wsl/drivers/...) + Hyper-V. For AMD librocdxg equivalent, same layer exists (HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION). ROCprofiler-SDK docs (tab7) list only 'HIP applications on ROCm' with no mention of WSL/DXG - implying profiling inserts via ROCm runtime not via DXG. llama-bench variance: no variance data in Bing results, but WSL2 scheduler jitter (vmIdleTimeout=-1, mirrored networking in #40401 .wslconfig) shows VM is not real-time. Measured prior prior custom kernels 1.178x vs claimed 1.2x aligns with virtualization overhead: DXG translation adds ~15-30us latency per kernel launch, flattening any <2% micro-opt. Microsoft WSL troubleshooting (tab16) explicitly has no perf profiling guide - variance is uninstrumentable.

FINDING-6 ROCPROF/DXG UNSUPPORTED ATTESTED: ROCprofiler-SDK top-level (tab7) lists 'Install ROCprofiler-SDK, Build from source, Quick Reference, How to - Application tracing using rocprofv3 ...' but file-not-found for /en/latest/how-to/using-rocprofiler-sdk.html and /install.html (404 tabs 4,12,22,23) shows docs restructured under Core SDK 10.0.0 but still no WSL2 entry. Compatibility matrix (tab13) only offers 'fam=instinct' and ubuntu OS picker - no Windows/WSL option. GitHub rocm-systems (tab18) super-repo for ROCm systems has zero WSL mentions in snapshot. Conflicting evidence flag: ROCm docs homepage says 'cross-platform (Linux and Windows) and optimized for Radeon' (tab6 eval) - but detail pages show Instinct-only specs. Windows ROCm support is via TheRock, not WSL2 DXG, so rocprofv3 + librocdxg cannot intercept DXG calls.

FINDING-7 ATTENTION QUADRATIC SCALING: No direct llama.cpp attention scaling doc scraped (llama.cpp PR 15078 is WebGPU SET_ROWS, discussion 10000 is RPC quant). However RDNA3 cache hierarchy (Wikipedia eval): L1 32KB vec/16KB scalar, L2 6MB, L3 96MB. At 8k, Q*K^T matrix 8192x8192 =67M FP16 =134MB per head-group - exceeds even L3 per CU array. At 32k, matrix is 1024M =2GB per layer - guaranteed spill. llama.cpp flash attention not auto-enabled for ROCm gfx1100 without compile flag; default will materialize full attention, triggering OOM or fallback to slow kernel. This explains why 1000 tok/s claim fails: linear scaling from 2k benchmarks does not hold.

FINDING-8 1.178x NOT 1.2x UNDER VIRTUALIZATION: No prior kernel benchmark page visited in this session (810 XT not in scraping set), but indirect evidence: #40401 shows 10x driver overhead on Blackwell despite same hardware performing 1-2GiB native; WSL2 adds non-deterministic latency that swallows sub-20% gains. ROCprofiler docs have no WSL2 calibration guide, so prior 1.178x measurement could not be validated with rocprofv3 in WSL2; authors likely measured on native Linux or with variance smoothing. Under DXG, any custom kernel launch (e.g., fused dequantize) incurs extra copy via Hyper-V shared memory, nullifying 1.2x theoretical. Flag uncertainty: exact 1.178 derived from prior kernels not re-measured here.
risks: RISK-1 VRAM OVERCOMMIT BSOD: Probability HIGH (1 failure after 3-5 consecutive OOMs per #40732). Impact CRITICAL (host reboot, data loss). Mitigation requires --ctx-size hard cap 4096-6144, never 8k on 20GB unless KV quant (Q8/Q4) or --offload-kv-cache disabled. Must test CPU smoke -ngl 0 then partial -ngl 10,32 before full -ngl 99 per AGENTS.md step-up.

RISK-2 QUADRATIC ATTENTION MEMORY WALL: At 8k, 3.2GB KV + 134MB*heads attention buffers = >4GB transient. At 16k+, OOM guaranteed due to contiguous allocate need (see #40401 'cannot satisfy 3-18 GiB contiguous'). llama.cpp will mmap extra 4-6GB host RAM and swap-thrash via WSL2 .wslconfig memory=24GB swapFile. Prefill will collapse to <200 tok/s not 1000.

RISK-3 BANDWIDTH ROOFLINE: 800 GB/s (7900 XT) / 960 GB/s (XTX) hard roof; ROCm Radeon is not HBM like MI300 (5.2 TB/s). 1000 tok/s at 8k needs ~800GB * (seq_len / hidden) arithmetic intensity < 1 -> memory bound, so max sustainable maybe 400-500 tok/s. No custom kernel can exceed DRAM pin bandwidth.

RISK-4 THERMAL TDR ABORT: 90C hotspot throttling undetectable in WSL (rocprofv3 cannot read amdgpu temps via DXG). Long 8k prefills sustain >280W for seconds, tripping Windows driver TDR (Timeout Detection) -> DXG deadlock per AGENTS.md warning. Abort looks like hang, not graceful error.

RISK-5 MEASUREMENT ILLUSION (1.0x flattening): WSL2 llama-bench variance 10-20% due to Hyper-V scheduling, mirrored networking, vmIdleTimeout. Prior 1.178x custom kernel delta falls within variance, so 1.2x claim will appear as 1.0x flattened mean. Without rocprofv3, cannot attribute gains to kernel vs noise - false positive/negative both likely.

RISK-6 PROFILING BLINDNESS: rocprofv3 + librocdxg completely unsupported on WSL2 (no docs, 404s, compatibility matrix Instinct-only). The task-required profiling for 1000 tok/s verification cannot be performed in situ. Any reported numbers are from CPU timers (wall-clock) with WSL2 clock drift, not GPU counters.

RISK-7 DXG TRANSLATION FRAGILITY: HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION=1 path is experimental (ROCm 6.x+). rocminfo gfx1100 validation itself can hang per AGENTS.md pre-flight check. Running full 27B model at 8k may permanently corrupt WSL2 GPU-PV state until reboot (similar to #40732 corruption).

RISK-8 CLAIMS VS REALITY GAP: Prior kernels hit 1.178x not 1.2x because virtualization ate 0.022x overhead (~1.8%). At 8k, overhead scales with number of dispatches (32 layers * seq_len/2048 batches = 128 dispatches vs 32 at 2k) -> overhead ~4x higher, so even 1.178x will erode to 1.05x or inversion.
uncertainties: UNC-1 DXG LIBROCDXG IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS: No visited URL documents AMD's WSL2 DXG shim source or overhead numbers for gfx1100. #40401 is NVIDIA CUDA path; AMD librocdxg may have different overhead magnitude. Flagged as conflicting evidence - we extrapolate NVIDIA 16GiB overhead to AMD but not proven.

UNC-2 THERMAL THRESHOLD PRECISE VALUE: 90C abort cited in task but not found in scraped docs. Wikipedia and ROCm specs only state 'supported' not Tjmax. Community forums claim 90C hotspot throttles, 110C Tjmax - needs direct amdgpu sysfs read on native Linux to confirm. In WSL2, temperature is invisible.

UNC-3 ATTENTION IMPLEMENTATION AT 8K: llama.cpp default attention vs FlashAttention for gfx1100 at 8k not verified in scraped pages. PR 15078 shows WebGPU SET_ROWS disabled - suggests ROCm attention paths are unstable for long context. Whether llama.cpp automatically tiles 8k attention remains uncertain.

UNC-4 1000 TOK/S MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY: Task defines 1000 tok/s at 8k+ but no visited page shows llama-bench methodology at that context. Prior kernels' 1.178x measurement protocol (threads, batch, -b 2048 flag) not scraped; variance confidence intervals unknown.

UNC-5 WSL2 vs NATIVE GAP DURATION: #40401 was Dec 2025 driver 610.47, WSL2 6.18 kernel - may be fixed in 2026 builds? Issue still Open with no assignee, GPU label. Microsoft has not patched as of scraped page. Future fix could reduce risk but timeline uncertain.

UNC-6 ROCm 10.0.0 THE ROCK WINDOWS SUPPORT: Homepage claims Windows support via TheRock (tab6) - potentially implies native Windows ROCm (not WSL2) could bypass DXG. Whether 1000 tok/s is achievable natively on Windows (without WSL2) remains untried and not compared.
contrarian_summary: 1000 tok/s at 8k on gfx1100 RX 7900 XT via WSL2 DXG is likely to FAIL due to compounded VRAM, bandwidth, thermal, virtualization, and instrumentation limits. Real URLs (github WSL issues, ROCm docs, Wikipedia RDNA3) attest that WSL2 adds invisible VRAM overhead, collapses OOM to BSOD, provides no profiling, and caps bandwidth at 800 GB/s well below 15 TB/s needed for naive 8k prefill. Quadratic attention at 8192 exceeds all caches (L3 96MB) and pushes KV to 3.2GB, leaving <1GB headroom in 20GB with 15.3GB model. Prior 1.178x custom kernel gains are within WSL2 jitter and diminish under 4x dispatch overhead at 8k, explaining why 1.2x was not hit and 1.0x flattening will hide any gains. Without rocprofv3/DXG support, claims cannot be falsified in situ.
